newsitem.title: GERMANY: Planned German chocolate price rise may be delayed.
newsitem.headline: Planned German chocolate price rise may be delayed.

text.p: Plans by German chocolate manufacturers to raise ex-plant prices of their products in the autumn may be unrealistic in a competitive environment, a spokesman for Kraft Jacobs Suchard (KJS) said.

"I believe the price rises may be delayed, perhaps until early next year, because none of the leading firms will step forward to be first, but that's my personal opinion," spokesman Rolf Sauerbier said in response to an enquiry.

German confectionery industry association BDS in a statement on July 8 tried to prepare the ground for retail price hikes, saying they might become necessary to reflect high futures, a weak mark and higher labour costs.
Chocolate makers have also complained about rising nut and almond prices.
The confectionery arm of the KJS group, part of Philip Morris, is the German market leader in 100 gram solid chocolate bars, with coffee and general food other areas of business.
Sales in the 100 gram market segment had been falling for several years and were set to ease again this year.
KJS, which has a 28 percent share, was forecasting an overall decline by 2,500 tonnes to 230,000 tonnes in 1997.
KJS prices of 0.95 marks per bar ex-plant are slightly above the present market average, which in 1996 was 0.91 marks.
KJS would take a closer look at its pricing structure but not before October partly because of a change in the top management of the chocolate division, Sauerbier also said.
Christian Koehler is due to take on the vacant position of general manager on August 1.
